item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israeli forces release Palestinian 'doctor of the poor ' with visible signs of abuse
item.description:
Israeli forces release Palestinian 'doctor of the poor ' with visible signs of abuse

Submitted by Bilge Kotan on Sun, 10/25/2026 - 18:54
The 71-year-old physician Mazen Rantisi was arrested in the occupied West Bank in June
Rantisi’s detention prompted widespread condemnation (Screengrab/X)
Off

Israeli forces released Palestinian doctor Mazen al-Rantisi, 71, from Ofer prison on Sunday after nearly four months in detention, with visible signs of physical abuse on his body.

In a photo circulated on social media after his release, the physician appeared gaunt, with a prominent red wound on his forehead.

Popularly described as the “doctor of the poor” for waiving fees, supplying medicines and operating a clinic that became a refuge for low-income Palestinians, al-Rantisi was detained in a pre-dawn raid on his home in Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on 21 June.

Prosecutors later indicted him for serving as chairman of the board of the Union of Health Work Committees, a Palestinian non-profit that provides medical care to thousands of Palestinians each year.

Al-Rantisi previously told his lawyers that he has suffered physical abuse and medical neglect in custody in Ofer prison, according to a Haaretz report. He also said the prison authorities withheld his regular medication for the first 10 days in Ofer prison and are still denying him one of his medicines.

Dr Ahmed Muhanna, who was released in January after 665 days in detention, told Healthcare Workers Watch (HWW) on Tuesday that “doctors have been singled out as targets for detention” and face particularly brutal treatment in custody.

Muhanna, who is the director of Al-Awda Hospital in Gaza, lost almost a third of his body weight while in detention. He said several of the Palestinian detainees died "as the […] Israeli jailers looked on", adding that the detained healthcare workers were prevented from helping other detainees, even those injured during violent interrogations.

"Israel’s continued detention of nearly one hundred healthcare workers is in clear contravention of International Humanitarian Law," Dr Rebecca Inglis, of HWW, said on Tuesday.

"We are gravely concerned for their welfare given the extensive evidence that Palestinian detainees are being tortured while in Israeli detention," she said.

Over 90 healthcare professionals remain detained 

According to HWW, 80 Palestinian healthcare workers from Gaza and 14 from the occupied West Bank remain in Israeli detention. Most were abducted by the Israeli military from their hospitals or ambulances while on duty.

Prominent doctors, including Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza, are among those who remain in Israeli prisons.

Abu Safiya was abducted from Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza in December 2024 after he defied Israeli orders to evacuate the hospital, which was one of the last functioning medical facilities in the Gaza Strip at the time. He has been held without charge since then.

A United Nations commission of inquiry said Abu Safiya faced “continued and severe abuse”, while his family and lawyer reported that he showed signs of severe torture.

According to Physicians for Human Rights, Abu Safiya told his lawyer in early September that guards beat him and threatened him, telling the doctor he cannot talk about the conditions he is being held in.

"The guards beat him in various parts of his body, including sensitive areas, using hands, feet and batons," the organisation and Abu Safiya's lawyer said.

Israeli forces have killed over 1,700 health workers and detained 364 since the start of the aggression, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

Six healthcare workers have died or been killed while in detention, and five more are missing, their whereabouts unknown, HWW said. The bodies have not yet been returned to their families.

Hebron is under full Israeli siege, mayor says

Israeli forces have sealed off all entrances to Hebron in the occupied West Bank and forcibly displaced around 2,200 Palestinians from their homes, Mayor Yousef Jaabari told Middle East Eye on Saturday evening.

“Hebron is now a disaster zone. The occupation has closed all entrances to the city. No one can enter or leave,” Jaabari said, accusing Israel of imposing collective punishment following a deadly shooting on Friday.

Two suspected Palestinians opened fire on Israeli troops at a checkpoint in northern Hebron early in the day near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint west of Hebron, killing two soldiers and wounding three others. 

Jaabari said Israeli forces forcibly evicted around 2,200 people, including elderly people, women and children, from Deir Bahala, al-Jalda and surrounding neighbourhoods. The affected area spans approximately 330 dunams and contains more than 490 housing units.

Residents told MEE that soldiers gave families five minutes to leave while videos posted on social media showed Palestinian lorry drivers working together to move goods and supplies out of factories ahead of their demolition by Israeli forces.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Lula defeats Bolsonaro in Brazil elections
item.description:
Lula defeats Bolsonaro in Brazil elections

Submitted by Mera Aladam on Mon, 10/26/2026 - 05:39
In a historic tight race, Lula secures fourth presidential term
Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva gestures as he addresses supporters after his victory in the presidential runoff election, at Paulista Avenue, in Sao Paulo, Brazil, 26 October, 2026 (Amanda Perobelli/Reuters)
Off

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva secured his fourth  non-consecutive presidential term late on Sunday, in a historic win against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

Lula won the tight race by 51.78% of valid votes against 48.22% for Bolsonaro, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

Heavy rain and technical issues had affected voting across the Latin nation, leading the country to keep open polls for two extra hours past 7pm local time (10pm GMT).

The defeated presidential candidate Bolsonaro announced he would call for the results to be annulled, citing the two-hour extension to voting given by the Supreme Court.

"We will engage our legal team and seek to have these elections annulled," he said. "I will not accept that the rules of the game have been arbitrarily changed—once again—by Lula’s friends on the Federal Supreme Court."

Bolsonaro's statement comes despite reports that the request for the extension was called for by both candidates, citing heavy rain and transport disruptions that prevented some voters from reaching polling stations.

Meanwhile, Lula's win marks the first time a presidential candidate in modern Brazilian history to have lost the first round of elections, only to win the second. 

Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro by more than three points in the second round of Brazil’s presidential election. https://t.co/NoLzGnJQ83

— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) October 26, 2026

His reelection challenges the current shift to right-wing politics across Latin America, where conservative governments have taken power in several countries. Lula's term is set to begin on 5 January, 2027.

Lula's left-wing politics

Throughout his political run, Lula has pursued closer cooperation with emerging economies and championed national sovereignty. 

During his presidency, Lula prioritised poverty reduction, social spending as well as environmental protection.

Unlike Bolsonaro, he has long been a critic of Israel and the US, calling for Palestinian statehood. The left-wing president has also backed strengthening ties with Iran and China. 

Following his victory, Lula said he wants to "make a commitment" and "will deliver the best term any president has ever served".

"I will dedicate myself 24 hours a day to making this the country that everyone dreams of," he told supporters. 

He also stressed national sovereignty, saying "in this election, we defeated the interference that was coming from the outside in." 

"Brazil is no one’s back yard," he added. 

Several countries and political figures have since backed Lula's win, including Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, United States Senator Bernie Sanders, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and several other leaders from across the region.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Brazil runoff live updates: world leaders congratulate Lula on historic election win as Bolsonaro refuses to concede
item.description:
Leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated the far-right senator and was elected president of Brazil for a fourth non-consecutive term

  • Full report: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil’s president over Flávio Bolsonaro

  • Live second round results

The local electoral court ordered the immediate restoration of 100% of the bus fleet and ordered the arrest of the municipal transport secretary, Pablo Souza, on suspicion of an electoral offence and disobeying court orders. The arrest warrant could not be carried out, however, because he is in Paris on what the city government described as an “official mission”, and is not expected to return to Brazil until Monday.

Late in the afternoon, Flávio Bolsonaro also filed requests for voting to be extended by two hours in cities in the states of São Paulo, Paraná and Santa Catarina, but because of heavy rain that he said had prevented voters from turning out.
